messages:
anya-peopleops: FYI — Carlos (SWE, offer accepted) just told us his spouse's consular appointment moved unexpectedly. Their visa stamping for the dependent and associated processing will now likely push his ability to travel to the US ~2–3 weeks. Current start date is May 12. What are our options for payroll, benefits, and getting him a laptop if we need to delay or allow a limited remote start?

miguel-peopleops: Thanks for the heads-up. Quick Q: does Carlos have any current US work authorization (EAD, H1B COS already approved but stamping pending, AP)? If not, payroll typically can't start until work auth is in place.

carlos-newhire: I don't have a visa stamp yet. H-1B change of status was approved inside the US earlier, but we had to travel to get the visa stamp and now spouse's appointment moved. I still have the COS approval notice (I-797).

immigration-legal: With an approved I-797 (change of status) + pending consular stamp, he should still be eligible to be paid if he's physically in the US and can complete Form I-9 showing lawful status. Problem is travel: without the stamp he may not re-enter the US if he leaves. Important: if he is currently in the US and has evidence of status (I-797), onboard as usual. If he's outside the US, we cannot pay/work until he has a valid visa to enter/work.

miguel-peopleops: Got it. So two scenarios: (A) Carlos is in the US now -> standard onboarding (I-9, payroll). (B) Carlos is outside US awaiting stamping -> we can't start payroll; options: delay start date or temporary contractor/consulting invoice (where legal approves). Which is it?

carlos-newhire: I'm currently outside the US — in Mexico — waiting for the new appointment. So likely scenario B. Sorry for the curveball.

anya-peopleops: No worries — thanks for clarifying. For scenario B here's what we can offer: 1) push start date until he has visa stamp + can enter US; 2) hire as a short-term contractor until stamping completes (requires legal + finance sign-off); 3) allow remote unpaid onboarding (docs, training) but not active payroll. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

immigration-legal: We generally avoid contractor route for new H-1B employees unless there's a clear lawful basis; I'll review risks but it's not preferred. Unpaid onboarding (access to docs, training) is fine as long as he doesn't perform billable work.

miguel-peopleops: OK — so likely approach: set a soft start for May 12 for orientation (unpaid, optional), set official payroll start once he has stamped visa and has re-entered. We should communicate benefits eligibility windows and relocation stipend timing.

anya-peopleops: Notes for benefits/payroll: - Benefits enrollment window opens on official payroll start date (benefits vendor requires active payroll enrollment). If we delay payroll, health insurance may not begin until first payroll cycle. - Relocation stipend can be paid after payroll start or as a reimbursable expense earlier (finance can expedite reimbursements case-by-case). - Equity grant vesting start is tied to official start date; we can make an exception on a case basis but need manager + People Ops approval.

raj-eng: Separate ask — if we delay payroll but want him to start training, can IT ship a laptop to his current address in Mexico? We need to confirm customs/shipping and asset rules.

it-ops-bot: IT checklist: need manager approval + shipping address + customs declaration (if shipping outside US). For asset tagging we require signed Acknowledgement before provisioning. If People Ops approves, we can ship a laptop but expect 7–14 business days to Mexico (depending on courier).

anya-peopleops: To move forward I'm sharing a short checklist for Carlos to complete and docs we need once he gets stamped. Copyable list below for candidate and manager:

```
Required for remote unpaid onboarding (no payroll):
- Manager approval for unpaid training (email thread saved)
- NDA & employment contracts signed
- Laptop shipping address + manager approval for international shipment
- IT Acknowledgement signed (digital ok)
- Tax/team orientation materials (no paid work until visa stamped)

Required to start payroll (employee in US):
- Passport + valid visa stamp (if travel required) OR I-797 showing change of status if already in US
- Completed I-9 documentation (we accept List A OR List C + D as applicable)
- Completed direct deposit form
- Signed offer paperwork confirmed
- Proof of address (for payroll/state tax)
```

anya-peopleops: Also drafting a short consulate courtesy letter template that the hiring manager can sign and Carlos can present if needed. Here's a one-paragraph sample (feel free to edit):

"Redwood Inference confirms that Carlos Lopez has an active employment offer for the role of Software Engineer with an intended start date of May 12, 2026. Due to an unexpected reschedule of a dependent consular appointment, the candidate's visa stamping appointment was delayed. We respectfully request that the Consulate consider available appointment slots and accommodate family scheduling constraints where possible. Redwood is committed to supporting timely completion of required immigration formalities."

immigration-legal: That template looks fine as a courtesy note — avoid making statements about back-dated employment or start dates for payroll. Keep it factual.

miguel-peopleops: Action plan so we're aligned: 1) I will email Carlos with the unpaid onboarding option + checklist today. 2) Legal will confirm contractor feasibility if Carlos prefers interim paid work (immigration-legal). 3) IT to confirm shipping estimate if manager wants laptop shipped. 4) People Ops to set tentative payroll hold and draft benefits communications.

it-ops-bot: To IT: please confirm shipping country customs code for laptop, ETA, and any prohibited items.

anya-peopleops: Owners and rough timeline: - Miguel: candidate comms + confirm unpaid onboarding by EOD today. - Immigration-legal: contractor risk memo by EOD tomorrow. - IT: shipping quote within 24 hours if requested. - Finance/Payroll: mark candidate as "hold" until stamped, prepare retroactive pay process if payroll needs to start earlier retroactively.

carlos-newhire: Thanks everyone — I appreciate the flexibility. I'll share the new appointment date as soon as it's confirmed and can sign the IT ack and NDA now.

anya-peopleops: Great — Miguel, loop Carlos into a doc with the checklist and attach the consulate note template. We'll reconvene when we have a confirmed appointment. :thumbsup:
